note: Re-judged 2026-10-11 by an independent judge after the fix round (2691e815b1). RFC 7296 3.5: "implementations MUST be configurable to send at least one of ID_IPV4_ADDR, ID_FQDN, ID_RFC822_ADDR, or ID_KEY_ID, and MUST be configurable to accept all of these four types." The send clause is proven under RFC7296-3.5-2 (buildIDPayload tests); this row's tests carry the accept clause. Positive TestRemoteIDAcceptsEveryMandatoryType (unchanged) requires checkRemoteIdentity to accept all four types under a configured remote-id, each with an anti-vacuity refusal of a wrong value, so refusing any of the four or short-circuiting on an empty remote-id fails. Negative TestRemoteIDRefusesTypesItCannotCompare: its claim now names ID_DER_ASN1_GN only, which is exactly what the body sends, and requires the not-comparable branch ("cannot compare") rather than a value mismatch, so a checker that accepts every type turns red; the earlier defect (claim naming ID_DER_ASN1_DN, which RFC7296-4-4 requires accepted) is resolved. Revert record on remote_id.go::assertedIdentity.
